we find that the next-to-leading-order correction to nucleon-nucleus scattering phase shifts is small and is model independent.

we have determined the next-to-leading-order contributions for two different leadingorder lattice actions, and that we find that the next-to-leading order corrections are accurate to the expected order of magnitude.

the study of the low energy properties of the nucleon-nucleus optical potential.
the application of chiral effective field theories (ChEFTs) to lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD).
the application of lattice methods to nuclear physics.

next-to-leading order is a necessary step in the lattice approach to the nucleon-nucleus problem.
chiral effective field-theory methods for the lattice are working as advertised.

chiral perturbation theory is a useful tool to describe nucleon-nucleus scattering on the lattice.

next-to-leading-order calculations of nucleon-nucleus scattering in the presence of a hard wall are feasible.
